why: The stable-lad says three of the sheep in the paddock have gone lame.
Holmes asks whether anything has been amiss with the sheep 'of late', and the lad answers about that period.
Holmes's sudden question and the lad's answer give the reader plain reason to wonder what lamed the sheep.

text: What lamed the sheep? — an epidemic or chance
why: An ordinary natural cause, illness or accident, is the obvious first thought for lame sheep.

text: What lamed the sheep? — someone practised on them
why: Nothing so far suggests anyone practised anything on the sheep; the label points at a solution the story has not yet revealed.
